changed.headline: Because of AI-supported intersection sensing, Bellevue, Washington's Safer Signals pilot cut near misses involving vulnerable road users by more than 45%.
Because of AI blind-spot cameras and coaching, Coach USA reports a 92% reduction in preventable incidents involving pedestrians, bicyclists and motorcyclists.
Because of AI airspace routing, the US Department of Transportation says the FAA's SMART tool helped reroute nearly 180 flights, improving flight times by more than 10 minutes each.
Because of AI road-defect detection on recycling trucks, City of Moreton Bay says 4,547 of the 12,896 potholes it repaired in six months were identified by AI.
Because of AI transit signal priority, San José says it increased bus speeds by 20 percent after expanding the system to all bus routes citywide.
Because of AI signal timing, West Allis, Wisconsin says all-day vehicle delay on W. Greenfield Avenue fell 25.2%, from 23.6 to 17.6 seconds per vehicle.
Because of machine-learning grid monitoring, PG&E says it avoided 12 million minutes of unplanned customer outages and intercepted 17 potential ignitions in 2025.
Because of AI occupancy-based ventilation control, a US children's hospital system cut HVAC energy use by 30 percent, according to the vendor R-Zero.
Because of AI satellite leak detection, Thames Water says a 19-week trial helped find more than 800 leaks, saving an estimated 8.7 million litres of water a day.

Because of AI-generated teaching images, medical students in a forensic medicine course in India scored higher on clinical reasoning than classmates who used conventional forensic photographs, in a non-randomized comparison.

In a pre-registered trial of 1,179 students in 10 UK secondary schools, Gemini tutoring inside the Eedi maths platform matched expert human tutors on in-platform measures but moved standardised Star Maths scores by only +0.02 standard deviations against standard remediation.
Because of AI call handling, Jeffcom 911 says it saw a sustained 33% reduction in administrative calls reaching its dispatchers.

A two-year cluster randomized trial in 18 Tennessee middle schools found that remedial-math students given Khan Academy with the Khanmigo AI tutor gained 1.3 national percentile ranks per term more than control grades, a small gain the authors say resembles Khan Academy practice without AI.

AI-assisted radiograph training did not significantly improve undergraduate dental students' diagnosis of proximal caries compared with conventional training, in a randomized study of 79 students in Saudi Arabia.
Not because of AI: prioritising abnormal chest X-rays with AI did not speed up lung cancer diagnosis across five NHS trusts in England, with median times of 44 days against 46 days.

An LLM math tutor given to middle-school students in Hamilton County, Tennessee helped them recover from mistakes and, inside a mastery workflow, scored 3.1 points higher on a delayed test of practiced material, a suggestive result.

Sending Pakistan's mobile TB X-ray camps to sites picked by AI did not find significantly more tuberculosis per camp than sites picked by field staff, across 3,936 camps and 269,254 people screened, in the trial's primary analysis.

Sumner County Schools in Tennessee says middle-school groups averaging 25 or more Coursemojo AI activities per student improved TCAP English proficiency by 3.7 percentage points, against -0.2 for groups with little or no use.
Because of AI, people in Tanzania with referable diabetic retinopathy were about twice as likely to reach the eye clinic within 8 weeks: 35.9% against 18.2% with standard screening.

Because of AI-drafted, dietitian-reviewed guidance, 66.7% of gastric and colorectal cancer surgery patients at one Wuhan hospital ate enough energy 30 days after discharge, against 40.0% given standard advice.

Because of AI, orthopedic surgery residents trained with a structured, faculty-supervised large-language-model framework scored higher on clinical reasoning in an unassisted final examination than residents taught the traditional way, in a randomized trial in Shanghai.

In a randomized crossover trial, 83% of 30 adults preferred a human-administered occupational therapy initial assessment to a remote AI-administered one, and rated the human format as more compassionate.

Because of AI, obstetrics and gynecology residents who trained with an AI virtual-patient platform scored higher on colposcopy case analysis after one month than residents on traditional teaching alone, in a randomized trial of 60 residents at two Chinese teaching hospitals.
Because of AI, community health workers in Andhra Pradesh, India, screened 7,879 people by cough sound and found 11 TB cases, 4 of them in people with no symptoms.

UC San Diego reports the failure rate in Foundations of Precalculus fell from 35.3% in Fall 2024 to 11.4% in Fall 2025 after a redesign that built in the ASPIRE AI tutor, a preliminary before-and-after figure.

leads_added: KITE-CRM, CT AI for cystic renal masses, randomized implementation of 5,869 adults at Changhai Hospital, Nov 2025–Feb 2026 (ChiCTR2500112290). [EClinicalMedicine](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eclinm.2026.104279). Benign treatment 28/2934 vs 104/2935 overall, but the AI-evaluable cystic subgroup was not significant (5/29 vs 19/56). Missing: full text, why treated counts differ (171 vs 258), and whether the overall gain came from lesions the AI never read.

AI vs teacher feedback on undergraduate essays, three-arm RCT, 312 students, Guangzhou, Sept 2025. [Frontiers in Psychology](https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1918748). Equal essay gains (d 0.60 vs 0.59 over no feedback), lower motivation with AI. Weak: not preregistered, one cycle, pre-window.

Suspected skin cancer referral rates after a pre-referral AI tool, real-world. [BJD](https://doi.org/10.1093/bjd/ljag496). Reader got HTTP 403, not read; may relate to `nhs-derm-skin-cancer`. Needs the full text, achieved dates, and comparison.
CT-based AI risk support for cystic renal masses, with a randomized component. [EClinicalMedicine](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eclinm.2026.104279). Already logged earlier and unreadable; still open.

Reducing benign breast biopsies in women 35 and under with a clinician-AI triage strategy. [Diagnostics](https://doi.org/10.3390/diagnostics16213491). Not read; likely retrospective. Check whether any patients were actually triaged.
Skipped: AEA registrations in development, reviews, benchmarks, model-accuracy papers, pharma-ads chatbot study, news and market pieces.
